messages.content: How do I raise my first round of funding in Lagos?

Before you talk to a single investor, you need three things: a working product with at least 10 paying users, a clear number on your monthly revenue growth, and a one-sentence answer to 'why you, why now, why this market.' Lagos investors have seen a thousand decks. They fund founders who have already started, not founders who are planning to start. What is your current MRR and growth rate?
My harvest income is seasonal. How do I budget for the lean months?

Divide your harvest income into three buckets the day it lands: 60% for the next planting cycle, 25% spread across the lean months as a monthly allowance, 15% into a savings group or mobile money you do not touch. The mistake most farmers make is spending harvest money like it is salary. It is not — it is 12 months of income arriving at once. How many lean months do you typically face before the next harvest?
How do I manage forex risk when importing from China?

Three moves: first, invoice in USD not RMB — you want one currency risk, not two. Second, pay your supplier within 30 days of the rate you quoted your buyer; every extra day is a bet you didn't choose to make. Third, build a 5% forex buffer into every landed cost calculation. What is your current payment cycle from order to customer delivery?
How do I get a loan without collateral for my small farm?

Your best options without collateral are: a chama or SACCO loan where your group membership is the guarantee, M-Shwari or KCB M-Pesa which lend based on your M-Pesa history, and government agri-credit schemes like AFC which have lower collateral requirements for smallholders. The fastest path is building your M-Pesa transaction history for 6 months — consistent deposits and withdrawals signal creditworthiness. How long have you been using mobile money and what is your average monthly transaction volume?
I keep spending all my salary before the month ends. What do I do?

The problem is not discipline — it is architecture. Your money has no structure so it flows to whatever is loudest. Fix this today: the moment your salary lands, move your savings first before you pay a single bill. Even ₦5,000. Then set fixed envelopes for rent, food, transport, and family obligations. What is left is what you actually have to spend. What does your salary look like and what are your three biggest monthly costs?
My supplier keeps raising prices. How do I protect my margins?

Raise your prices immediately — today, not next week. Every day you absorb the supplier increase is a day you are paying your customers' bills. Calculate your new landed cost, add your margin, and update your price board. Your loyal customers will understand. The ones who leave over a small price increase were never your real customers. What is your current margin on this product?
How do I turn my music into a sustainable income in Accra?

Streaming alone will not pay your rent in Accra — the per-stream rates are too low for the market size. Your income stack needs to be: live performances (highest margin), sync licensing for ads and films, merchandise, and brand partnerships. The artists making real money here treat music as the marketing and live shows as the product. How many shows are you doing per month right now and what are you charging?
I'm a photographer. How do I price my work properly?

Stop pricing by the hour and start pricing by the outcome. A wedding client is not buying 8 hours of your time — they are buying the only record of the most important day of their life. Price that. Calculate your costs: equipment depreciation, editing time, travel, storage. Add a 40% margin minimum. Then research what the top 3 photographers in your city charge and position yourself deliberately. What is your current average booking fee?
